chunks: ‘Alī ibn Muḥammad, from his father, raising it, said:
A man said to Abū ‘Abdillāh عليه السلام: “Indeed, the sun rises between the two horns of al-Shayṭān.”

He said: “Yes. Indeed, Iblīs has taken a throne between the heaven and the earth. So when the sun rises and the people prostrate at that time, Iblīs says to his devils: Indeed, the children of Ādam are performing salat for me.”

key_terms.إِبْلِيسَ: Iblis, the chief devil speaking to his devils
key_terms.السَّمَاءِ: the heaven, part of the realm between which Iblis places his throne
key_terms.الشَّمْسَ: the sun, mentioned here in connection with the time of rising
key_terms.الشَّيْطَانِ: al-Shaytan, the satanic being associated with misguidance
key_terms.سَجَدَ: prostrated, referring to the act of سجدة
key_terms.عَرْشًا: a throne, indicating a place of satanic stationing
key_terms.قَرْنَيِ: the two horns, part of the expression describing al-Shaytan
key_terms.يُصَلُّونَ: they perform salat, meaning they are praying

ai.seo_question: Why is it said that the sun rises between the two horns of al-Shaytan?
ai.summary: This hadith describes a cosmological image connected to the rising of the sun and the claim of Iblis over acts of prostration done at that time. It highlights the spiritual significance of proper worship and the danger of actions that can resemble devotion directed to other than Allah.
